Yes, you were. But our oven is one of these built-in things and it dates from the 1970's and isn't even in temperature at all. They don't make a size to replace it with and so we get by with it until we can redo the kitchen. Above it is a 1975 microwave (we still have the original manual) that we use for storage. Fun times!

I'll give you a tip: modern ovens can be adjusted if you read the manual, BUT you can still be handy with older ovens by buying an oven thermometer. Put it on the center oven rack, then set the dial for 250F. Wait 20 mins, and look at the thermometer. Make a note of any discrpancy between the set temp and the temp on the thermometer. Now change the setting to 300F. Wait another 20 mins and do the same thing. Same for 350, 400, and 450.

What you'll usually find is that if it's inaccurrate, it's usually by the same amount(which surprised me, I thought it would be a percentage), like 20 degrees too hot at every setting.

Even if it doesn't work out that simply, you can still get an idea of what you need to do, like add 5 degrees when you set it to less than 300, subtract 10 degrees when over 375....

I did that in my current oven, and found it was about 10 degrees too hot always. Downloaded the manual, learned how to make the adjustment, performed the test again.... bullseye every time. My daughter did that in hers, and it was already accurate.

Oven thermometers are fairly cheap, like 10ish dollars. You can usually find them in a grocery store in the section where they sell kitchen utensils.
